video_caption: A man with long dark hair, a beard, and a red baseball cap worn backward sits in a black chair in front of a dark red wall adorned with framed posters and figurines, including a white skull-like object. He is wearing a grey t-shirt with a warrior graphic and speaks into a microphone positioned to his left, which has a fuzzy wind screen and several colorful stickers, including yellow smiley faces. Between 0:14 and 0:16, the video rapidly zooms in on his face, his eyes widen dramatically, and his head appears to spin with a blurred, swirling background effect. He then returns to speaking directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands, at one point pointing toward the upper right corner of the screen as if indicating a button, and later gesturing as if closing a window. The video then cuts to a black screen displaying white text that reads: "The 2nd Grooming Allegation June 17th 2022".

A man with a beard and long dark hair, wearing a red baseball cap backward and a dark gray t-shirt, is speaking directly to the camera from a dark chair. A microphone, adorned with several colorful pins/buttons, is positioned in front of him. The background is a dark red wall with framed artwork and a white skull-like object visible on a shelf to the right. At 0:02, the screen transitions to display a news article on the left side, while the man continues to speak in a smaller frame on the right. The headline of the article reads: "Massachusetts court grants temporary protection order against actor Ezra Miller." The sub-heading below it states: "The actor has now been asked to appear in court in two states after parents accused them of grooming, abuse and intimidation involving a nonbinary child, 12, and a nonbinary adult, 18." Below the text, a black and white close-up image of a person's eyes and nose (Ezra Miller) is partially visible. The man on the right gestures with his hands as he speaks, and at 0:17, the screen returns to showing him full-frame, where he continues to speak and gesture with his hands to emphasize his points.

The video displays a split screen, predominantly showing a news article on the left and a man on the right. The article, titled "By Kat Tenbarge," describes a Massachusetts mother receiving a temporary order of protection for her 12-year-old child against actor Ezra Miller. The text states: “A Massachusetts mother has been granted a temporary order of protection on behalf of her 12-year-old child against Ezra Miller, the 29-year-old actor who stars in the upcoming Warner Bros. superhero movie “The Flash.” The court order, issued Wednesday by the Greenfield District Court in Massachusetts and seen by NBC News, said it “was issued without advance notice because the Court determined that there is a substantial likelihood of immediate danger of harassment.” The order does not contain any allegations against Miller." (meaning: A Massachusetts mother obtained a temporary protection order for her 12-year-old child against Ezra Miller, the 29-year-old actor from "The Flash." The court issued this order without prior notice due to a high likelihood of immediate harassment. However, the order itself does not include specific accusations against Miller.) The man, with a beard and long dark hair, wears a red cap backwards and a dark t-shirt. He sits in front of a dark red wall decorated with framed pictures, reading the article text aloud into a microphone. Throughout the segment, he uses various hand gestures, including pointing his right index finger, and animated facial expressions to emphasize parts of the article. Twice, the video cuts to a close-up of the man, where he points directly at the camera with an intense expression before returning to the split-screen view.

The video features a man with long dark hair and a beard, wearing a red baseball cap backward and a dark grey t-shirt with a graphic, speaking into a black microphone adorned with colorful stickers. He sits in a black desk chair against a dark red wall, decorated with framed posters and artwork, including one partially visible that says "DRAGON'S." The video alternates between showing him full-screen and showing him in the bottom right corner with an article text filling the rest of the screen. He gestures with his hands as he speaks, his expression serious at times, and he smiles slightly towards the end of the segment. The visible text from the article discusses a mother's concerns about Ezra Miller's relationship with her child: "The mother, who spoke on the condition that their names be withheld out of privacy concerns, said she and her child met Miller in February through an acquaintance. She said Miller first seemed friendly but that she soon grew suspicious of Miller's relationship with her child. She said she told the judge that Miller offered to buy the child gifts, including a horse, even after she rejected Miller's earlier offers. “I kept wondering why Ezra was here. Like, don’t you have Hollywood stuff to do? Don’t you have movies coming out?” she said. The order of protection, first reported by The Daily Beast, adds to what is now a three-month series of a that started with disorderly conduct grown to include accusations from pa allegations against Miller have also p Miller’s aggressive fan base that main people calling for the authorities and". The man is reacting to and commenting on this article.

A man with a beard and mustache, wearing a red baseball cap and a dark t-shirt, is shown speaking into a microphone and looking towards a screen displaying a news article. He appears to be reacting to the article, with his mouth open as if mid-sentence. Behind him, various posters or collectibles are visible on the wall, suggesting a casual room or studio setting. A white text box is overlaid on the lower left portion of the screen, partially obscuring the man, displaying the headline "Actor Ezra Miller arrested twice in less" and the timestamp "20, 2022 / 00:20". The main article text, which the man is likely reading or discussing, details a "three-month series of allegations directed at Miller that started with disorderly conduct charges in Hawaii and has since grown to include accusations from parents of child grooming. The allegations against Miller have also prompted online furor pitting Miller's aggressive fan base that maintains their innocence against people calling for the authorities and Warner Bros. to take action."

The video opens with a black screen displaying white text that reads "DC/WB Response" and "June 17th 2022" (DC/WB Response June 17th 2022), accompanied by a dramatic sound. It then transitions to a split screen: on the left, a "DEADLINE" news article headline reads "Zaslav's First Movie Crisis: What To Do With Ezra Miller, The Erratic Star Of Warner Bros' $200M 'Flash' Franchise Launch," with two small images below – a red Flash helmet and a water tower. On the right, a man with long dark hair, a beard, and wearing a red baseball cap backwards and a dark t-shirt, sits in a chair in front of a microphone, looking at the article, nodding and saying "Yikes." The scene then shifts to a full shot of the man, who is now speaking directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands as he explains his thoughts, with a red wall adorned with various framed posters and a white skull decoration visible behind him.

The video begins with a split screen, featuring a news article from "DEADLINE" on the left and three images above it: a close-up of a red and green costume, a water tower, and two people at a desk. The article's headline states that "The Flash is becoming Warner Bros Discovery CEO David Zaslav's first movie crisis, because of the escalating coverage of incidents of volatile and odd behavior involving the film's star, Ezra Miller." Below the article, the speaker, a man with a beard, long dark hair, and a red cap worn backward, is visible from the chest up, sitting in a chair with a microphone in front of him. He is wearing a dark t-shirt and looks at the camera, talking. He then brings his hands together in a prayer-like gesture, and continues to speak, using hand gestures to emphasize his points. He suggests that "grooming multiple children" is "a little bit more than odd behavior" and advises "DEADLINE" to "upgrade that to like creep behavior, illegal behavior, possibly map behavior." As he talks, a video clip appears on the right side of the screen showing Ezra Miller on a red carpet, wearing a white cape and a mask of their own face, moving their head around. The speaker clarifies that this particular act is "odd" but acceptable if one wants to be a "crazy actor." The video then transitions to grainy footage, watermarked "TMZ," first showing three people on a street, with Ezra Miller (wearing a green jacket) in the middle, and then shifting to a dimly lit, club-like setting where Ezra Miller (in a white shirt) appears to be moving erratically. The speaker is then shown again, looking directly at the camera and pointing his finger, reiterating his point about the severity of the alleged actions.

The video opens with a split screen, featuring a white webpage with black text on the left and a man speaking in the bottom right corner. The text on the webpage discusses Johnny Depp's replacement by Mads Mikkelsen in the *Fantastic Beasts* franchise after a UK lawsuit, and mentions a studio source stating, “There is no winning in this for Warner Bros… This is an inherited problem for Zaslav. The hope is that the scandal will remain at a low level before the movie is released, and hope for the best to turn out.” Further text, partially obscured, refers to Ezra Miller in the Flash role and a $200 million film. The man, wearing a red baseball cap backward, a dark grey t-shirt with a graphic design, and sporting long dark hair and a beard, is seated in a black chair. He looks slightly to the viewer's left, speaking into a black microphone adorned with stickers, and occasionally gestures with his right hand near his mouth. The background is a dark red wall with framed pictures or posters. Around the 0:10 mark, the video zooms in, filling the frame with the man, who then raises his right index finger for emphasis before continuing to gesture with his hands as he speaks directly to the camera, maintaining a serious but engaged expression.

The video opens with a split screen, featuring a news article on the left and a man speaking on the right. The article's headline refers to an "inherited problem for Zaslav" and discusses a "scandal" related to the "Flash role in future DC films," mentioning a "$200 million investment" and "Warner Bros execs have to be cringing." An advertisement with the text "FOR YOUR CONSIDERATION OUTSTANDING OR ANTHOLOGY" is partially visible below the article. The man, wearing a red baseball cap backward and a dark grey t-shirt with a graphic, has long dark hair and a beard, and is seen animatedly speaking into a microphone with a black furry cover. His background is a dark red wall adorned with various framed posters and a white mask. At 00:18, the shot transitions to a close-up of the man, who continues to gesture and speak directly into the camera. Finally, at 00:28, the screen cuts to black with white text that reads: "DC Fucks up their own shit (everyday)".

A man with long dark hair, a beard, and wearing a red baseball cap backward and a dark gray t-shirt featuring a white graphic of a warrior, sits and speaks into a black microphone on a stand to his left. He gestures with his hands, at times pointing with his right index finger, against a dark red wall adorned with framed posters and various collectibles. From 00:10 to 00:27, the scene transitions to a comic book cover titled "DC THE FLASH: THE FASTEST MAN ALIVE!" (English), depicting the red-suited Flash on the ground while a muscular, naked man with light skin and brown hair pulls at his suit, surrounded by lightning bolts. In the upper background, Batman flies and a police car is airborne. During this comic book display, the man speaking is visible in a small inset video in the bottom right corner, continuing to react and make hand gestures. The video then cuts back to the full shot of the man, who finishes speaking directly to the camera with expressive hand movements.

The video opens with a man with a beard and long dark hair, wearing a red baseball cap backward and a dark grey t-shirt, sitting in a black gaming chair. He looks directly at the camera, speaking and using his hands for emphasis, pointing his right index finger, then gesturing downwards with both hands, and finally making a "thank you" gesture with his hands together. A black microphone with several colorful pins is positioned on a stand to his left. The background features a red wall adorned with framed comic book posters and, to the right, a white Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles mask on a shelf. The scene then transitions to an animated background of a dark, starry night sky with a large, glowing red and orange sun-like orb partially obscured by purple clouds near the horizon, reflecting on a purple, wavy surface below. Large white text "SUBSCRIBE" appears in the center of the screen, followed by a list of names scrolling upwards under the heading "THANK YOU CHANNEL MEMBERS," which are the names of his supporters. As the names scroll, the man's voice can be heard thanking each channel member individually, referring to them as "chads." The list continues to scroll throughout the segment, featuring names like "OM3G4 WOLF," "DEX LUTHER," "DARTH VADER," and "ANGRY GOAT," among many others, all in white text against the vivid red and purple background.
